newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour's Clark will negotiate to lead new govt.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour's Clark will negotiate to lead new govt.

text.p: New Zealand opposition Labour leader Helen Clark said she would negotiate with the aim of leading a new government after Saturday's general election.

"I will be endeavouring to negotiate to see that I can lead a change of government and certainly leadership of this country is something that I would consider a great honour to accept," Clark told supporters.
"I know that many people have expressed the hope that I will break through that glass ceiling and be the first woman prime minister of New Zealand," Clark said.

Latest television projections gave Labour 36 seats in a new 120-member parliament, indicating it was capable of forming a government if it gains support from nationalist New Zealand First, with 17, and the left-wing Alliance, with 13.
The conservative National Party, in power since 1990, was projected to gain 45 seats and its potential coalition partner, radical free-market Act New Zealand, was on course to win eight.
